results.summary:
hkb init now registers the checkout it just set up in the user-level board list (~/.config/hkb/boards.json): a step 7 in src/init.js calling registerUserBoard(root) through a new registerCheckout() helper, at the end of a successful run.

Behaviour: idempotent (the helper compares resolved paths, so a second init — or a checkout somebody already listed by hand — adds nothing); never silent (one line either way, `registered this checkout in <file> — hkb serve will show it` or `already listed in <file> …`, which is the disclosure that init wrote a file outside the repo, so there is deliberately no --no-register flag); never fatal (a malformed or unwritable list prints a warning naming the path to add by hand and init still exits 0, leaving a hand-written file byte-identical); and the offline `--no-labels --repo owner/name` path registers too, since it is a local write.

`hkb init --json` gained its first stdout payload: {repo, board, root, registered: {file, added}}. init's human log has always gone to stderr, so that object has stdout to itself; the test parses the whole of stdout from the real binary.

Judgement call a reviewer should look at: the entry is a BARE path — registerUserBoard(root), letting `board` default to null — not `path#board`. init has just written the slug into .kanban/board.json and contextForPath reads a bare entry's slug from there, so both resolve identically today and a bare entry follows a later rename. The deciding reason is dedupe: a bare resolved path is the spelling the README tells people to hand-write, so registering a checkout already on the list adds nothing instead of a second card on the serve page.
